The question we had not asked until this week is whether both agents read the same amount of that file. They do not, and the reason is a unit. Codex budgets project instructions in bytes. title: Claude Code Put Your Email in the User-Agent Header
content: Originally published at webofmike.com on 2026-11-15. On November 5, someone opened anthropics/claude-code#107757 with one line that explains the whole problem: "I receive dozens of scam emails per day because claude code divulged my email to arbitrary 3rd parties in the User-Agent request header while conducting web searches without my permission." The issue hit Hacker News at 1388 points and 437 comments within a day. Anthropic had already shipped a mitigation three days earlier, and commenters found a hole in it before the HN thread even cooled down. I reproduced both the leak and the bypass in a small repo, agent-egress-header-scrub , and it points at an argument I keep making on this site: a check that lives inside the agent has to anticipate every way a value could reach the network. A check at the network boundary only has to look at what actually leaves. title: Schema-Enforced JSON Never Failed Parsing; Getting There Cost Three Times the Tokens
content:
A post called "Your Agent Needs a Schema, Not a Better Prompt" has been climbing the AI tag this week, and it's the kind of claim I usually see argued from vibes rather than numbers. I run git_commit.py in my my-git-manager repo, a script that shells out to claude -p and asks for a one-line Conventional Commit message as plain text, no schema involved. I'd never actually tried the alternative on my own machine, so I built a small side-by-side test instead of taking the trending post's word for it. The claude CLI has a --json-schema flag I hadn't used before: --json-schema <schema>   JSON Schema for structured output validation

author: Enjoy Kumawat

title: Claude Office Party Enables Linux Code Execution
content: A fixed temporary-file path in Claude's official document-processing skills can cause LibreOffice to load and execute an attacker-supplied shared library on Linux. The code runs with the privileges of the user operating the AI agent. AIR Security found the flaw, named Office Party, in Anthropic's DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX skills. These skills let Claude create, read, edit, and process Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, and Excel spreadsheets. Anthropic acknowledged the issue after AIR reported it in May but considers it outside its security boundary because the affected code runs inside a sandbox. The helper script remains unchanged, according to the researchers. A predictable library becomes executable input The vulnerable component is soffice.py , a helper script that starts LibreOffice for document conversion, including rendering Word documents as PDFs. In environments where LibreOffice cannot open Unix-domain sockets, the script falls back to a workaround based on Linux's LD_PREL

title: Stop Claude Code from overwriting your .env with a PreToolUse write guard
content: Permission deny rules can stop Claude Code from reading .env and key files. That still leaves a hole: a Write or Edit call can create or overwrite those paths. A small PreToolUse hook closes it. The hook Save this as .claude/hooks/block-secret-writes.sh and make it executable ( chmod +x ): #!/usr/bin/env bash # Reads the tool call as JSON on stdin; exit code 2 blocks it. path = $( jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.path // ""' ) if echo "$path" | grep -Ei '\.env([.-]|$)|\.(pem|key|p12|pfx)$|private.?key|id_rsa|wallet|mnemonic|credentials?' ; then echo "Blocked: '$path' looks secret-bearing. Do not let the agent write credentials, keys, or wallet material." >& 2 exit 2 fi exit 0 Register it in .claude/settings.json so it only runs on file writes: { "hooks" : { "PreToolUse" : [ { "matcher" : "Write|Edit" , "hooks" : [ {

The timing makes sense. Two things changed at once: models got better at judging when to act and when to ask, and intelligence got cheaper. On one long-horizon coding benchmark, Opus 5.5 cost 78% less per solved task than Opus 5 — 40% less on typical workloads. When every wake-up costs a fraction of what it used to, an agent that wakes up on its own stops being a luxury and starts being a design pattern. But the first thing to get straight is the name. title: MCP vs CLI: MCP 서버가 컨텍스트 윈도우를 빠르게 소모하는 이유
content: MCP vs CLI: 도구 정의 토큰이 컨텍스트 윈도우를 얼마나 먹어치우는가 MCP vs CLI의 핵심은 에이전트가 언제 도구에 대한 비용을 지불하느냐에 있습니다. MCP 서버는 사용자가 아무것도 입력하기 전에 모든 도구의 이름, 설명, JSON Schema를 모델에 전송합니다. 반면 CLI는 에이전트가 실제로 실행해서 --help 나 출력 결과를 읽기 전까지는 아무 비용도 들지 않습니다. 측정된 환경에서 네 개의 일반적인 MCP 서버는 11,923개의 도구 정의 토큰을 추가한 반면, Apidog CLI 스킬은 112토큰만 추가했습니다. 오늘 Apidog를 사용해 보세요 이 격차가 바로 이번 주에 발행된 두 개의 Dev.to 게시물의 배경에 있는 전부입니다. 한 개발자가 코딩 에이전트에 "Run tests"라고 입력했더니 파일도 첨부하지 않았고 히스토리도 없는데 첫 요청에서 28,400개의 입력 토큰 이 소모되는 것을 보았습니다. 원인은 일곱 개의 MCP 서버였습니다. 또 다른 개발자는 MCP가 너무나 간단해서 만들기 쉽다 는 점이 바로 문제라고 주장하며, 어려운 부분들(인증, 승인, 중복 호출)은 데모가 동작하는 순간부터 시작된다고 말했습니다. 이 글은 한 가지 질문에 집중합니다. 도구 정의가 컨텍스트 윈도우에 얼마나 비용을 발생시키며, 에이전트가 필요할 때 호출하는 CLI는 언제 더 적은 비용을 들일까요? 만약 문제가 거대한 도구 응답이라면, 비대해진 API 응답 줄이기 에 관한 자매 포스트를 읽어보세요. MCP 서버는 왜 컨텍스트 윈도우 토큰을 소모할까 MCP 서버는 tools/list 메서드를 통해 자신의 도구를 알립니다. MCP 도구 사양 에 따르면 각 도구는 name , description , inputSchema (인자에 대한 JSON Schema)를 가집니다. 모델이 도구를 선택하려면 클라이언트가 이러한 정의들을 요청에 넣어야 합니다. 전통적인 구성에서는 에이전트가 도구를 호출하든 아니든, 모든 대화의 매 턴마다 이 작업이 일어납니다. 따라서

title: Researchers Decrypt Hidden Chain-of-Thought From OpenAI, Anthropic and Google APIs
content: LLM providers return hidden reasoning as encrypted blocks, but those blocks work across sessions, users and models. Feeding one into a weaker sibling model makes it print the trace in plaintext. The authors used this to recover 367 PII artifacts and 182 credentials from public logs, and they propose mitigations. Read All

title: Brecha de Cursor: la clave de Fireworks abrió la cadena
content: La brecha de Cursor empezó con una clave de Fireworks. Con la clave, el atacante copió datos de un depósito de almacenamiento de solo lectura que Cursor usaba para compartir información con Fireworks. title: Anthropic Launches Claude Haiku 5.5 — Its Fastest Model Yet for High-Volume Tasks
content: Anthropic announced Claude Haiku 5.5 on November 13, and Gadgets 360 reports it's the fastest model the company has released to date. This isn't a flagship launch. Haiku is the small, quick tier of the Claude family — it sits below Sonnet and Opus — and version 5.5 doubles down on the one thing that tier exists for: pace. Every major lab keeps a model like this in the catalogue, and there's a reason. The heavyweight models handle the hardest reasoning, but the everyday traffic of an AI product — the sorting, summarising, fetching and tidying — runs on the small tier. When that tier gets faster, everything built on top of it quietly gets faster too. Built for bulk work The reported target list is refreshingly unglamorous: summarisation, classification, database queries and context compaction. That's the background work of modern AI products — tickets sorted by the thousand, documents condensed as fast as they're uploaded, plain-English questions fired at databases all day long. Context

title: Você não precisa de superpoderes. Precisa de contexto.
content: Toda tecnologia nova traz junto um pacote de metodologias prontas prometendo te ensinar a usá-la do jeito certo. Não seria diferente com os agentes de IA. Basta abrir o LinkedIn pra ver alguém instalando um plugin aleatório que promete transformar o Claude Code num time inteiro de engenheiros. Brainstorm, SDD, TDD, subagente revisando subagente. E aí a pessoa muda a forma que trabalha há vinte anos pra caber dentro do fluxo do plugin. Isso funciona com muitas pessoas? Sim, mas se você é um dev experiente, você já acumulou uma bagagem absurda que pode e deve ser amplificada com os agentes ao invés de recomeçar do zero. title: AI Loves Purple: Most and Least Used AI Colors
content: Ask any AI coding tool for a landing page and watch what happens. A dark hero section. A glowing card or two. A button that fades from indigo into purple. Ask again with different words and you often get the same thing. If you have noticed this, you are not imagining it. Developers have been joking about "the purple problem" for more than a year, and the creator of Tailwind CSS publicly apologized for his part in it. But the jokes hide a more useful question: which colors does AI actually use the most, which does it use the least, and what can you do about it when you ship real products? This guide breaks down the colors most used by AI, where they come from, and the exact steps to replace them in your own code. We answer that with a clear line between three kinds of evidence: what was actually measured, what is well documented history, and what is designer observation. Then we give you code you can use today to find and replace AI default colors in your own projects. The Short Answer

title: Sonnet 5.5 vs Sonnet 5: When To Reach For Which
content: If you are choosing between two adjacent Sonnet versions for the same job, the useful questions are what each costs per call, how fast each is, and how much of the prompt each gets from cache. We have figures for both from our own use. Over the last 90 days, two Anthropic models handled book.questions.solver across 453 calls: Sonnet 5.5 took 337 of them and Sonnet 5 took 116. title: Your AI Agent Doesn't Need Another API Subscription. It Needs a Wallet.
content: An API subscription is a pricing model built for a human who logs in every morning. Your agent doesn't log in. It has no favorite tab, it renews nothing, and it has never once clicked "Remind me later". It buys 1 call at a time , in bursts, in the middle of the night, from a tool it may never touch again. content: Human approval is not a security boundary unless it is bound to the exact action being approved, enforced at execution time, and protected against replay. A system that fails to meet these conditions can be vulnerable to attacks, even if the model is not malicious. Read All
